text:
maya: Quick sync on the routing policy editor UI. Main pain points from yesterday's usability session: users confused by the 'Stack' label, keyboard reorder loses focus, validation badges are vague, and the preview sim doesn't indicate which rule fired. Posting gifs and a prototype shortly.

jess: Heard. Can we capture a thread of proposed small changes so we can scope a 1-2 sprint fix?

thomas: Re: label, +1 to use 'Priority' — aligns with our API and docs. Also the drag handle needs better contrast and a larger hit target. Consider showing a grab affordance (vertical bar) on hover.

oliver: Copy suggestions: replace "No conflicts" with "No conflicting rules detected" and change terse errors like "Invalid sequence" to descriptive ones e.g. "Priority conflict: rule 2 and rule 5 share priority 10." Add a small link "How to fix" that expands inline.

lia: Accessibility: keyboard reordering currently moves the DOM node but focus jumps to body. We should keep focus on the moved item and announce the new index via an aria-live region. Also add aria-labels to the drag button and make the suggested badge accessible. Example implementation snippet attached.

sam: Preview sim idea: make the sim a mini-trace rather than a black-box result. Show input -> each rule evaluated (pass/fail) -> matched rule highlighted -> output. Keep it collapsed by default with a compact toggle. This will help debug fuzzy rules.

designbot: Uploaded: priority-editor-proto-2026.gif and contrast report. The current dot-handle (color #8f8f8f) is failing for small sizes. Suggest #4a4a4a and increase size to 20px touch area. Also suggested motion for reordering so users see the displaced rows.

maya: For validation UI, I'm trying an inline pill that appears under the offending rule with a link to the conflicting rule. Example copy: "Priority overlap with 'Holiday banner' — click to jump". Thoughts on jumping vs showing both? Jumping seems fastest.

jess: Jumping is fine, but add a short toast/backlink so users can return to previous spot.

thomas: Edge case: auto-suggested optimizer rules. Where do they land and how do we show provenance? Propose: place them below user rules with a blue "Suggested" badge and a tooltip: "Added by optimizer; editable". Keyboard users must be able to opt-out.

lia: Accessibility nit: badges need text equivalents and focusable tooltips. For suggested rules, ensure the tooltip can be opened with Enter/Space when focused.

oliver: Also propose microcopy for the preview trace toggle: "Show evaluation trace (helps debug why a rule matched)". Keep language action-oriented.

sam: I'll mock a compact three-column trace: Inputs | Evaluation steps | Outcome. The matched step gets a green check and a border. When collapsed, show a one-line summary: "Matched: rule 3 - send to model-X".

maya: Action list: 1) rename 'Stack' -> 'Priority' + update docs (thomas), 2) increase handle contrast & hover affordance (thomas/designbot), 3) implement aria-live reorder announcement + keep focus (lia), 4) richer validation copy + "How to fix" links and jump (oliver), 5) preview trace collapsed by default + matched-step highlight (sam), 6) suggested-badge pattern for optimizer rules (sam/oliver). I'll collate PRs into one epic.

thomas: I'll do rename and handle styling today.

lia: I'll prototype keyboard flow and share test notes tomorrow.

oliver: I'll prepare copy variants and the small help blurb.

sam: Mockups inbound by EOD.

designbot: Tickets created: RD-UX-4502 (priority rename), RD-UX-4503 (handle contrast), RD-UX-4504 (preview trace). :white_check_mark:

maya: Thanks team! I'll post the prototype link and assign follow-ups in the epic. :sparkles:
